Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask. We can provide both artifacts and outline the exception flow. Quick summary up front:

- Redaction sample: we can produce a CSV sample showing raw -> redacted output for three representative debug-record types (user prompts, request metadata, and telemetry traces). The sample will include deterministic pseudonymization for user IDs and full removal or hashing for sensitive tokens.
- Deletion manifest: we use a standard per-tenant manifest that records object ids, deletion timestamps, retention policy applied, and signed hash proof-of-delete. We'll attach the template and a short explanatory note.
- Temporary retention exception: Redwood supports customer-scoped temporary retention windows (up to 90 days for staging/forensics) but these require an internal approval (security + legal) and an attestation package (SOC 2 evidence + SIG submittal for the change). For a 45-day exception we typically: submit a request record, capture justification, owner, SRE mitigation controls, and provide a signed attestation plus sampling of deletion APIs post-window.

Looping in Marissa for the actual artifacts and Karthik for technical notes about ephemeral debug traces and KV cache behavior. We'll aim to get the attachments and a one-page exception runbook to you before EOD.

Thanks,

Hi Sophie — attaching the artifacts Neha mentioned and a short primer below. See the attached files: acmeedge-redaction-sample.csv (synthetic examples), deletion-manifest-template.pdf, debug-log-scope-mapping.xlsx.

Primer:
- Redaction approach: for debug traces we apply a classification + rewrite pipeline. PII fields (email, phone, SSN-like patterns) are replaced with stable pseudonyms when the customer requests pseudonymization; session tokens and API keys are always removed. We leave non-sensitive telemetry intact to preserve observability. The attached CSV shows three sample rows: original, redaction result, and transformation tag.
- Deletion manifest: the template includes columns for object path, tenant id, retention policy id, deletion action, deletion timestamp (ISO), and a SHA256 proof-of-delete. When we complete deletion we deliver the manifest and a signed statement (PDF) for customers doing regulated erasure.
- Temp retention exceptions: operationally we create a scoped change with an expiry timestamp and an owner. During the exception we do two things to reduce risk: (1) ensure stricter access controls (role elevation only for named engineers) and (2) schedule automated purge jobs to run at expiry. After expiry we run a verification (sample exports + hash-checks) and provide a short attestation. For SOC 2/SIG purposes we include the exception request record, mitigation controls, and the proof-of-delete sample in the evidence bundle.

Notes on KV cache & streaming state: transient KV cache entries used to accelerate streaming generation are considered ephemeral and are not part of persistent tenant exports. Persistent debug traces are stored in a tenant-scoped debug bucket and subject to the TTL policy (default 30 days). If you need staging to keep 45 days, the exception will be limited to that bucket and will not alter production retention defaults.

Let us know the specific tenant IDs (or staging vs prod) and we'll populate the sample manifest for AcmeEdge.

Thanks,
